findings.reason: the matplotlib half of §1 may be an rcParam change rather than a new module and style field, or the plan must state why path.simplify_threshold cannot reach the size and vertex target.
findings.text: §1 adds a new imas_ink/_decimate.py min/max envelope and asserts the 1.7–3.4 MB SVGs come from "every one of up to 310,077 cached samples per trace ... written as a path vertex", but matplotlib already decimates drawn paths to display resolution through rcParams["path.simplify"] / "path.simplify_threshold": measured on the repo's own venv, a 300,000-sample SVG line is 300,071 vertices / 7.4 MB with simplify off, 8,948 vertices / 232 KB at the default threshold 0.1111, and 1,053 vertices / 37 KB at threshold 1.0 — below the plan's own 4,000-vertex target. The plan cites no search and no comparison against this existing knob. The altair path (_render_timeseries_alt, imas_ink/alt.py:370) has no equivalent, so the module is still needed there.

findings.reason: the section must account for the render_mpl keyword surface, or thread the flag to the private renderer without adding public surface, to meet the one-rule interface budget.
findings.text: §2's stated mechanism, that time_trace_figure_mpl "passes label_time=False for every panel but the bottom one", can only reach _render_timeseries_mpl (imas_ink/mpl.py:549) through the exported dispatcher render_mpl (exported at imas_ink/__init__.py:112 and :288; called at imas_ink/figures.py:95 and :100), so it adds a keyword parameter to a public function; §2 nevertheless says "It adds no public name" and names nothing retired or merged. (The §1 trace_max_points InkStyle field IS accounted for — the section states why nothing can be retired — but §2 is not.)

findings.reason: the plan names the altair stack and deliberately scopes it out with a stated reason (a served MCP application, not the matplotlib figures this plan serves).
findings.text: the "stack traces on one shared time axis" concern has a second owner: the altair trace stack sets one "Time [s]" x-title per trace (imas_ink/alt.py:393) and concatenates one chart per panel (imas_ink/server/mcp.py:296–299), reproducing at alt.py:393 the same repeated-label defect §2 fixes at imas_ink/mpl.py:577, while §1 is willing to edit alt.py for decimation but §2 leaves this path unchanged.

duplicate_owner-1.reason: repeat of the v0 finding declined with reason: the repeated altair title arises where the served MCP application concatenates charts in server/mcp.py, outside the matplotlib figures this plan serves

interface_budget-1.reason: plan v2 §2 has time_trace_figure_mpl call the private renderer directly for every panel, so the exported render_mpl gains no keyword

reuse_search-1.reason: plan v2 §1 uses matplotlib's path.simplify_threshold for the matplotlib half, set by render_to_bytes from a new InkStyle.path_simplify_threshold (1.0), and keeps the min/max envelope only for altair, which has no equivalent

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — imas_ink/_decimate.py is one private function hiding the bin/min-max envelope behind an interface smaller than what it hides, shared by both renderers.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the shared-time-axis concern has a second owner in the altair stack (imas_ink/alt.py:393), which §2 leaves repeating the label.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a keyword to the exported render_mpl yet states it adds no public name and names nothing retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1 adds a new decimation module without citing matplotlib's existing path.simplify_threshold, which already reduces an SVG path to display resolution.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §2 extends the existing _render_timeseries_mpl label mechanism rather than adding a parallel wrapper over it.
